name: The New Cadavre Connection
caption: A unit billed by NPWA NANET in the surviving 1997 Usenet record.

tenures.note: Held the NPWA World Tag Team Championship entering 1997 (won 24 Dec 1996); retained a Texas Tornado defense at Valentine's Day Massacre '97; lost the title to the Muslim Massacre at April Assault (11 Apr 1997).

name: The Muslim Massacre
caption: Col. Mustafa and Gen. Arain's own pairing, winning the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the New Cadavre Connection at April Assault and losing it to the Lords of the Ring that June.

tenures.note: Won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the New Cadavre Connection at April Assault (11 Apr 1997; Resident Evil flew Vegas to London on the Concorde to turn on the champions mid-show); lost it to the Lords of the Ring by 23 Jun 1997. Managed by The Sheik.

name: The Lords of the Ring
caption: Won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship by June 1997, losing it to the Asian Triad at Armageddon '97 that August.

tenures.note: Won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship by 23 Jun 1997 (debuted 24 Feb 1997, an outsider's-eye vignette watching Valentine's Day Massacre '97 by satellite in England); lost the title to the Asian Triad at Armageddon '97 (3 Aug 1997, a Triangle Tag Match also involving the Hell Razors).

name: The Asian Triad
caption: Akira Sasaki and Kenshin Nobunaga's own pairing, NPWA World Tag Team Champions after a Triangle Tag Match win at Armageddon '97 until Gan Green and the Maltese Falcon took the title back that September.

tenures.note: Won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship in a Triangle Tag Match over the Lords of the Ring and the Hell Razors at Armageddon '97 (3 Aug 1997); lost it by 18 Sep 1997 to Gan Green & the Maltese Falcon.

name: The Perfect Role Models
caption: A unit billed by NPWA NANET in the surviving 1997 Usenet record.

tenures.note: A recurring comedy tag team across the whole held corpus from Nov 1996 (Traction Zone, Thursday Night Thrashings) through Xmas Gory '97 -- self-billed 'Nanny Award' winners, the pairing behind the Valentine's Day Massacre '97 kayfabe-breaking comedy fall (already served) and a running presence across April Assault, Inhuman '97 and Summer Games. Never recorded holding an NPWA title in the held record.

name: New Wave of Wrestling (NWW)
caption: A title-holding stable fronted by Colonel Buddy Lee Jarrett, running the NPWA Television and North American Championships through its own members across 1997.
notes: Named directly in the fed's own text ("the entire New Wave of Wrestling," "the NWW"). Jurisprudence held the Television Championship and Steve Stone the North American Championship as NWW's own men through much of the run (see reigns.json, both already on record); the Fishmonger manages the group's own wrestlers rather than competing himself.

tenures.source: served shows across the year, e.g. /promotions/npwa-nanet/archive/npwa-april-assault-1997-04-11.html, /promotions/npwa-nanet/archive/npwa-armageddon-1997-08-03.html

name: Green World Order
caption: An nWo-parody stable that invaded a single St Patrick's Day 1997 NPWA card for a green-liveried, one-night tag title challenge, referenced in NPWA's own broadcasts through the rest of the year.
notes: Led by Hollywood Cheat Cheat Rodriguez; its in-ring pairing 'the Greensiders' (Mr. Big Wrestling Cool and Da Gan Green Guy, i.e. Gan Green) challenged the Cadavre Connection for the NPWA World Tag Team Titles on the St Patrick's Day 1997 Monday Night Mayhem (1TCHiwxizKYJ, CGyeZKwabZ8J, SQrjoA-jWB8J, h5lzTKln8g4J) and lost by outside interference from Resident Evil; Mucous 'Barf' Jobwell won the card's own first-ever Leprechaun Match for the group, and Mr. Freestyle disguised himself as Breakfast Bobby Toast ('gWo Bobby') to ambush an opponent. The five-member roster is named in full on a commemorative-plate merchandising gag at April Assault (Akx89RsXhVIJ, 11 Apr 1997), recapped in the May Markazine review (Fnl6eIDhFQgJ). On 12 Jul 1997, New Wave of Wrestling leader Col. Buddy Lee Jarrett offers founding member Gan Green a spot in the New Wave, referencing the Green World Order's own formation 'a few months ago' (4vwliOlKaJYJ, npwa-thursday-night-thrashings-1997-07-10.html). The gimmick drew in-fiction criticism as a stale copy of other federations' angles from two other wrestlers on the immediately following week's Thursday Night Thrashings and was still referenced on a fan sign eight months later at the 10 Dec 1997 Monday Night Mayhem (hT6vKhtSQucJ). The same source lead's citation of msg_id Akx89RsXhVIJ as 'not yet served' is also superseded: direct check confirms it was already served, as part of the April Assault PPV's own main-card range.

name: The Outcast Rogues
caption: A Japanese tag team who won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship on 29 Sep 1998 and lost it two weeks later at the wing's own 5th Anniversary Special.

tenures.source: recurring across the held record's May 1998 six-man tag scene; won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the Masters of Disaster, Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; lost the belts to the Asian Revolution in a Double Jeopardy six-man match, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998.

name: The Masters of Disaster
caption: A Philadelphia tag team managed by Tank, NPWA World Tag Team Champions through most of mid-1998 and North American Tag Team Champions from November 1998.

tenures.source: billed reigning NPWA World Tag Team Champions, referenced retaining against the Outcast Rogues via Armageddon V footage (6 Sep 1998) before losing the belts to the Rogues outright, Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; won the newly-created North American Tag Team Championship from Assault and Battery at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998.

name: The Cult
caption: A three-man stable (Locutus, Doctor Death, Father Armageddon) and the first NPWA North American Tag Team Champions, with Locutus standing in for Armageddon in the ring.

tenures.source: billed reigning NPWA North American Tag Team Champions (Doctor Death & Father Armageddon on the belts, Locutus wrestling in Armageddon's place), retaining against the Larson Brothers, Mayhem 6 Oct 1998; lost the belts to Assault and Battery, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998.

identity.note: The name 'The Cult' is carried by unrelated stables in other wings (osw, agw), with no shared evidence. Held distinct under the no-auto-merge rule.

name: Assault and Battery
caption: A Richmond, Virginia tag team, managed by Jen, who won the NPWA North American Tag Team Championship in their first pay-per-view match and lost it in their next.

tenures.source: won the NPWA North American Tag Team Championship from The Cult, Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998, billed undefeated in NPWA tag competition; lost the belts to the Masters of Disaster at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998, their first loss, after a masked interloper knocked out Eddie Simpson for the pin.

name: The Asian Revolution
caption: A Japanese tag team who won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship from the Outcast Rogues in a Double Jeopardy six-man match at the wing's 5th Anniversary Special.

tenures.source: named as rivals to the Outcast Rogues entering Mayhem 29 Sep 1998; won the NPWA World Tag Team Championship (teamed with "Breakfast" Bobby Toast in a Double Jeopardy stipulation) at Mayhem 5th Anniversary Special 13 Oct 1998; retained against the Rogues at Hell On Earth, 1 Nov 1998.

name: Final Justice

tenures.source: Tagged NPWA in the RSPWF Top 200 Tag Teams for 1998.

caption: Ranked #86 in the RSPWF Top 200 Tag Teams for 1998 (Adam Barney & Mike Hall), tagged NPWA.

identity.note: The registry's own decorated-aka guard reads this name as a normalized substring match against final-justice, justice-pccw. Recorded distinct, not merged: the only record this entity has is a placing in the RSPWF Top 200 Tag Teams, which gives a team name, a federation tag, and (where named) its two members' ring names, and nothing else -- no dates, no roster, no URL, so three of the collision doctrine's own four signals are simply absent and the no-merge default holds. Every held-promotion roster the ranked names were checked against came back with zero overlap. Reopenable the moment either side gains a record the other can be checked against.
